 Former NC State football head coach Chuck Amato passes away at 80
 Chuck Amato, a former NC State head coach and the only coach to lead the Wolfpack to double-digit wins in a single season, has passed away at the age of 80 after a long battle with throat cancer.
 R. Cory Smith 48 RALEIGH, N.C. -- Former NC State  football coach and Wolfpack legend Chuck Amato has passed away at the age of 80. The legendary Wolfpack coach previously battled with throat cancer and passed away after being in hospice care for several months.
 Amato served as the NC State head coach for seven years, four of which were with Philip Rivers as the quarterback. He reached five bowl games in those seven seasons, finishing with a 49-37 (25-31 ACC) overall record and earning four bowl wins. His best year with the Wolfpack was in 2002, when he helped guide the Wolfpack to an 11-3 record and a Gator Bowl victory over Notre Dame .
 During his time in Raleigh, Amato helped the Wolfpack get 20-plus players drafted to the NFL, including first-round selections like Rivers, Mario Williams, Manny Lawson and John McCargo . Williams was the only player in Wolfpack history to go No. 1 overall in the modern era of the NFL after a breakout season with the Wolfpack under Amato's defense in the 2006 NFL Draft.
 Known by Wolfpack faithful as "Chuck the Chest," Amato was a larger than life personality for the Wolfpack during his time. His time in Raleigh produced several legendary players in the red and white, but also saw assistant coaches like National Champion Curt Cignetti , ACC Champion Manny Diaz , C-USA Champion Doc Holliday , NFL head coach Marc Trestman , Norm Chow and several others go on to have head coaching careers.
 Prior to his coaching days with the Wolfpack, Amato played linebacker for NC State under legendary head coach Earle Edwards from 1965-67. Amato was a captain for the defense as a senior in 1967 and won multiple ACC Championships as a wrestler at heavyweight, going undefeated in 1966 and 1968.
 He then returned to the Pack to get his start in coaching as a grad assistant under Al Michaels and Lou Holtz , eventually serving as a defensive backs coach under Holtz and a defensive coordinator with Bo Rein until 1979.
 Amato then went on to coach at Arizona for two seasons before starting a long stint with Florida State under another legendary head coach in Bobby Bowden . The two worked together for nearly two decades from 1982 through 1999, with Amato coaching the defensive line for four seasons before taking over as the associate head coach and coaching either the defensive line or linebackers until he left for NC State prior to the 2000 season.
 Following his coaching career that ended at Akron in 2017, Amato returned home to Raleigh and hosted The Chuck Amato Show from Amedeo's prior to our live shows in the same room. Amato was truly a 1-of-1 personality and changed a room when he walked into it. Our thoughts and prayers go out to his wife, Peggy, his daughters, LuGina and Selena, and the entire Amato family. He was beloved by the NC State family and no one will ever replace that legendary raspy voice that roamed the Wolfpack sidelines.
